title: Nieuwland et al. 2018: Multi-site N400 Replication Study
description: A large-scale multi-laboratory replication study (N=356 participants across 9 UK institutions) investigating probabilistic prediction in language comprehension using event-related potentials (ERP). Participants read sentences word-by-word while EEG was recorded, with critical manipulations of indefinite articles (a/an) preceding expected or unexpected nouns. The study tests whether readers pre-activate phonological forms of predicted words, replicating and extending DeLong, Urbach & Kutas (2005). Raw EEG data from multiple recording systems (BioSemi, BrainVision, Neuroscan) are provided in BIDS format with enriched event metadata including cloze probabilities and stimulus characteristics.
methods_description: EEG was recorded during a word-by-word rapid serial visual presentation (RSVP) task at 2 words per second (200 ms word duration + 300 ms blank). Participants read 80 replication sentences and 80 control sentences with indefinite articles preceding either high or low cloze probability nouns. Comprehension questions were presented on a subset of trials requiring yes/no button responses. Data were collected across 9 laboratories using different recording systems (BioSemi BDF, BrainVision, Neuroscan CNT) with sampling rates ranging from 250–2048 Hz and 32–128 EEG channels plus peripheral channels.
